criteria: Russian revolutionary populists (Narodniks) of the 1860s-1880s whose substantial political activity belonged to that movement or its direct organisations (Chaikovsky Circle, 'going to the people', Zemlya i Volya, Narodnaya Volya, Chorny Peredel), including key theorists. Later Marxist or SR careers do not remove the earlier period, but people whose populist phase was trivial, writers or historians who merely wrote about the movement, nihilists/anarchists not identified as populists, and Tsarist officials targeted by it are excluded.
